        return a == b

def excel_like_equal(a, b):
    """Approximate COUNTIF equality for plain text/number criteria."""
    if is_blank(a) and is_blank(b):
        return True
    if is_blank(a) or is_blank(b):
        return False

    # Numeric comparison, including numeric strings.
    try:
        if isinstance(a, str):
            a_num = float(a.strip())
        else:
            a_num = float(a)
        if isinstance(b, str):
            b_num = float(b.strip())
        else:
            b_num = float(b)
        return a_num == b_num
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        pass

    # COUNTIF text matching is case-insensitive for normal text.
    return str(a).lower() == str(b).lower()

# Detect the contiguous source table headers starting at column A, stopping at the first blank header.

value_to_count = ws_values["I2"].value

for c in source_cols:
    if excel_like_equal(ws_values.cell(row=1, column=c).value, header_to_match):

        # Treat rows with any source-table content as data rows; this supports variable row counts.
        if all(is_blank(ws_values.cell(row=r, column=c).value) for c in source_cols):
            continue
        if excel_like_equal(ws_values.cell(row=r, column=match_col).value, value_to_count):
            result += 1

# Modify only the answer cell.
ws["I3"] = result

os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(output_path), exist_ok=True)
wb.save(output_path)

# Verification output

check_ws = check_wb.active
print("I3 =", check_ws["I3"].value, "type:", type(check_ws["I3"].value).__name__)
